simple.text: Fiziologiya hayotning fizik-kimyoviy mexanizmlarini tuşuntiradi. Organizm ~35–40 trillion hujayradan iborat “ijtimoiy tuzum”: har bir a’zo **hujayradan taşqari suyuqlik (ECF) — içki muhit** (Claude Bernard, *milieu intérieur*) doimiyligini saqlaşga hissa qöşadi; bu **gomeostaz** (Walter Cannon, 1929). Içki muhit me’yorda bölsa hujayralar yaşaydi; bir tizim işdan çiqsa — hamma hujayra zarar köradi (örtaça disfunksiya = kasallik, oğir = ölim).

items.text: **Hujayralar:** qizil qon hujayralari ~25 trillion (eng köp tur). Içakda 400–1000 tur mikrob (*microbiota*) — inson hujayralaridan köp (p.8).

**Suyuqliklar:** kattalar tanasining 50–70% suyuqlik; ~2/3 hujayra içida (ICF), ~1/3 taşqarida (ECF). ECF: Na⁺, Cl⁻, HCO₃⁻, O₂, glyukoza, yoğ kislotalari, aminokislotalar, CO₂. ICF: K⁺, Mg²⁺, fosfat (p.9).
**Me’yor — qiymat emas, diapazon.** Qondagi H⁺ özgarişi <5 nmol/L; Na⁺ bir neça mmol/L ga özgaradi — bu H⁺ dan ≥1 mln marta katta (p.9).

**Kasallikdagi gomeostatik kompensatsiya:** masalan, buyrak tuz çiqara olmasa → arterial bosim oşadi → çiqariş me’yorlaşadi, lekin uzoq muddatda bosim a’zolarni (buyrakni ham) şikastlab, ayovsiz doira hosil qiladi (p.9). Patofiziologiya şu “savdolaşuv”larni örganadi.

**Qon aylaniş** — ECF ni ikki bosqiçda taşiydi: tomirlar böylab va kapillyar–interstitsiy almaşinuvi (diffuziya). Qon tinç holatda butun aylanani ~1 marta/min, faol holatda 6 martagaça ötadi. Hujayralarning kami kapillyardan >50 µm uzoqda — diffuziya soniyalarda (Fig. 1-1, 1-2).
**Ozuqa manbalari:** öpka (alveolyar membrana 0,4–2,0 µm), oşqozon-içak, jigar va metabolik a’zolar, muskul-skelet tizimi (harakat orqali oziq topiş/himoya).
**Çiqindilarni çiqariş:** öpka (CO₂ — eng köp metabolit), buyrak (filtratsiya + kerakli moddalarni qayta söriş; moçevina, kreatinin yomon söriladi), içak, jigar (zararsizlantiriş, safro).

**Boşqaruv:** asab tizimi (sensor kiriş → MNS integratsiya → motor çiqiş; avtonom qism içki a’zolarni ongsiz boşqaradi) va gormonlar (tiroid — reaksiyalar tezligi, insulin — glyukoza, adrenokortikal — Na⁺/K⁺/oqsil, paratgormon — Ca/fosfat).
**Himoya:** immun tizim (özini-begonani farqlaş, fagotsitoz/antitelolar), teri (çegara, harorat, ajratiş).
**O₂:** gemoglobinning **kislorod-bufer** funksiyasi — töqimada O₂ köp bölsa bermaydi, kam bölsa beradi.
**CO₂:** yuqori CO₂ nafas markazini qözğatadi → çuqur, tez nafas → CO₂ çiqariladi.

**Arterial bosim — baroreseptor refleksi** (Fig. 1-3): uyqu arteriyasi bifurkatsiyasi va aorta ravoğidagi çöziliş reseptorlari → uzunçoq miya (set point bilan soliştiriş, “xato signali”) → vazomotor markaz tormozlanadi → simpatik faollik ↓ → tomir kengayadi, yurak kuçi ↓ → bosim pasayadi; aksinça ham.

**Table 1-1** — ECF tarkibiy qismlari, me’yor va ölimgaça bölgan çegaralar. Misollar: harorat me’yordan atigi 7°C (11°F) oşsa — ayovsiz doira; pH me’yor 7,4, ölimli qiymatlar ±0,5; K⁺ me’yorning 1/3 dan pastga tuşsa — falaj, 2 baravardan oşsa — yurak depressiyasi; Ca²⁺ yarmidan pastda — tetaniya; glyukoza yarmidan pastda — asabiylik, tutqanoq (p.13).
**Manfiy qayta aloqa** — köpçilik tizimlar: oğiş uni bartaraf etuvçi javobni çaqiradi.

**Kuçaytiriş koeffitsienti (gain) = tuzatiş / qolgan xato.** Misol: baroreseptorsiz bosim 100→175 mm Hg, baroreseptor bilan atigi +25 mm Hg; tuzatiş −50, xato +25 → gain = −2 (buziliş 1/3 gaça kamayadi). Harorat nazorati gain ≈ −33 (ança samarali) (p.13–14).

**Musbat qayta aloqa — “ayovsiz doira”** (Fig. 1-4): 2 L qon yöqotilsa → bosim ↓ → koronar oqim ↓ → yurak zaiflaşadi → ... → ölim; 1 L da manfiy qayta aloqa yengadi va tiklaniş böladi. Yurak me’yorda ~5 L/min haydaydi.

**Foydali musbat qayta aloqa:** qon ivişi (iviş omillari kaskadi; notöğri bölsa — aterosklerotik pilakçada tromb → infarkt), tuğruq (baçadon böyni çözilişi → kuçliroq qisqariş), nerv impulsi (Na⁺ kanallarining oçilişi özini kuçaytiradi). Har doim umumiy manfiy qayta aloqa jarayonining bir qismi.
**Oldindan boşqariş (feed-forward)** va **adaptiv nazorat** (keçiktirilgan manfiy qayta aloqa) — tez harakatlarda miya oldindan buyruq beradi, keyin sensor axborot asosida keyingi safar tuzatadi.

full.text: Physiology is the science that seeks to explain the physi cal and chemical mechanisms that are responsible for the origin, development, and progression of life. Each type of life, from the simplest virus to the largest tree or the complicated human being, has its own functional char acteristics. Therefore, the vast field of physiology can be divided into viral physiology, bacterial physiology, cellular physiology, plant physiology, invertebrate physiology, ver tebrate physiology, mammalian physiology, human physi ology, and many more subdivisions.

The science of human physiology attempts to explain the specific characteristics and mech anisms of the human body that make it a living being. The fact that we remain alive is the result of complex control systems. Hunger makes us seek food, and fear makes us seek refuge. Sensations of cold make us look for warmth. Other forces cause us to seek fellowship and to reproduce. The fact that we are sensing, feeling, and knowledgeable beings is part of this automatic sequence of life; these spe cial attributes allow us to exist under widely varying con ditions that otherwise would make life impossible.

Human physiology links the basic sciences with medicine and integrates multiple functions of the cells, tissues, and organs into the functions of the living human being. This inte gration requires communication and coordination by a vast array of control systems that operate at every level—from the genes that program synthesis of molecules to the complex nervous and hormonal systems that coordinate functions of cells, tissues, and organs throughout the body. Thus, the coor dinated functions of the human body are much more than the sum of its parts, and life in health, as well as in disease states, relies on this total function. Although the main focus of this book is on normal human physiology, we will also discuss, to some extent, _pathophysiology,_ which is the study of disor dered body function and the basis for clinical medicine.
CELLS ARE THE LIVING UNITS OF THE BODY
The basic living unit of the body is the cell. Each tissue or organ is an aggregate of many different cells held together by intercellular supporting structures.

Each type of cell is specially adapted to perform one or a few particular functions. For example, the red blood cells, numbering about 25 trillion in each person, trans port oxygen from the lungs to the tissues. Although the red blood cells are the most abundant of any single type of cell in the body, there are also trillions of additional cells of other types that perform functions different from those of the red blood cell. The entire body, then, contains about 35 to 40 trillion human cells. The many cells of the body often differ markedly from one another but all have certain basic characteristics that are alike. For example, oxygen reacts with carbohydrate, fat, and protein to release the energy required for all cells to function. Furthermore, the general chemical mecha nisms for changing nutrients into energy are basically the same in all cells, and all cells deliver products of their chemical reactions into the surrounding fluids.

Almost all cells also have the ability to reproduce addi tional cells of their own type. Fortunately, when cells of a particular type are destroyed, the remaining cells of this type usually generate new cells until the supply is replenished.

In addition to human cells, trillions of microbes inhabit the body, living on the skin and in the mouth, gut, and nose. The gastrointestinal tract, for example, normally contains a complex and dynamic population of 400 to 1000 species of microorganisms that outnumber our human cells. Communities of microorganisms that inhabit the body, often called _microbiota,_ can cause diseases, but most of the time they live in harmony with their human hosts and provide vital functions that are essential for survival of their hosts. Although the importance of gut microbiota in the digestion of foodstuffs is widely recognized, additional roles for the body’s microbes in nutrition, immunity, and other functions are just beginning to be appreciated and represent an intensive area of biomedical research.
full.lead: Microorganisms Living in the Body Outnumber Human Cells.

full.text: EXTRACELLULAR FLUID—THE “INTERNAL ENVIRONMENT”

About 50% to 70% of the adult human body is fluid, mainly a water solution of ions and other substances. Although most of this fluid is inside the cells and is called _intracellu lar fluid,_ about one-third is in the spaces outside the cells and is called _extracellular fluid._ This extracellular fluid is in constant motion throughout the body. It is transported rapidly in the circulating blood and then mixed between the blood and tissue fluids by diffusion through the capil lary walls.

In the extracellular fluid are the ions and nutrients needed by the cells to maintain life. Thus, all cells live in essentially the same environment—the extracellular fluid. For this reason, the extracellular fluid is also called the _internal environment_ of the body, or the _milieu intérieur,_ a term introduced by the great 19th-century French physi ologist Claude Bernard (1813–1878).

Cells are capable of living and performing their spe cial functions as long as the proper concentrations of oxygen, glucose, different ions, amino acids, fatty sub stances, and other constituents are available in this inter nal environment.

The extracellular fluid contains large amounts of sodium, chloride, and bicarbonate ions plus nutrients for the cells, such as oxygen, glucose, fatty acids, and amino acids. It also contains carbon dioxide that is being transported from the cells to the lungs to be excreted, plus other cel lular waste products that are being transported to the kid neys for excretion.
full.lead: Differences in Extracellular and Intracellular Fluids.

full.text: The intracellular fluid contains large amounts of potas sium, magnesium, and phosphate ions instead of the sodium and chloride ions found in the extracellular fluid. Special mechanisms for transporting ions through the cell membranes maintain the ion concentration differences between the extracellular and intracellular fluids. These transport processes are discussed in Chapter 4.
HOMEOSTASIS—MAINTENANCE OF A NEARLY CONSTANT INTERNAL ENVIRONMENT

In 1929, the American physiologist Walter Cannon (1871–1945) coined the term _homeostasis_ to describe the _maintenance of nearly constant conditions in the internal environment_. Essentially, all organs and tissues of the body perform functions that help maintain these relatively con stant conditions. For example, the lungs provide oxygen to the extracellular fluid to replenish the oxygen used by the cells, the kidneys maintain constant ion concentra tions, and the gastrointestinal system provides nutrients while eliminating waste from the body.

The various ions, nutrients, waste products, and other constituents of the body are normally regulated within a range of values, rather than at fixed values. For some of the body’s constituents, this range is extremely small. Varia tions in the blood hydrogen ion concentration, for exam ple, are normally less than 5 _nanomoles/L_ (0.000000005 moles/L). The blood sodium concentration is also tightly regulated, normally varying only a few _millimoles_ per liter, even with large changes in sodium intake, but these varia tions of sodium concentration are at least 1 million times greater than for hydrogen ions.

Powerful control systems exist for maintaining concen trations of sodium and hydrogen ions, as well as for most of the other ions, nutrients, and substances in the body at levels that permit the cells, tissues, and organs to perform their normal functions, despite wide environmental varia tions and challenges from injury and diseases.

Much of this text is concerned with how each organ or tissue contributes to homeostasis. Normal body functions require integrated actions of cells, tissues, organs, and multiple nervous, hormonal, and local control systems that together contribute to homeostasis and good health.

_Disease_ is often considered to be a state of disrupted homeostasis. However, even in the presence of disease, homeostatic mechanisms continue to operate and maintain vital func tions through multiple compensations. In some cases, these compensations may lead to major deviations of the body’s functions from the normal range, making it diffi cult to distinguish the primary cause of the disease from the compensatory responses. For example, diseases that impair the kidneys’ ability to excrete salt and water may lead to high blood pressure, which initially helps return excretion to normal so that a balance between intake and renal excretion can be maintained. This balance is needed to maintain life, but, over long periods of time, the high blood pressure can damage various organs, including the kidneys, causing even greater increases in blood pressure and more renal damage. Thus, homeostatic compensa tions that ensue after injury, disease, or major environ mental challenges to the body may represent trade-offs that are necessary to maintain vital body functions but, in the long term, contribute to additional abnormalities of body function. The discipline of _pathophysiology_ seeks to explain how the various physiological processes are al tered in diseases or injury.

This chapter outlines the different functional systems of the body and their contributions to homeostasis. We then briefly discuss the basic theory of the body’s control systems that allow the functional systems to operate in support of one another.
EXTRACELLULAR FLUID TRANSPORT AND MIXING SYSTEM—THE BLOOD CIRCULATORY SYSTEM

Extracellular fluid is transported through the body in two stages. The first stage is movement of blood through the body in the blood vessels. The second is movement of fluid between the blood capillaries and the _intercellular spaces_ between the tissue cells.

**Figure 1-1** shows the overall circulation of blood. All the blood in the circulation traverses the entire circuit an average of once each minute when the body is at rest and as many as six times each minute when a person is extremely active.

As blood passes through blood capillaries, continual exchange of extracellular fluid occurs between the plasma portion of the blood and the interstitial fluid that fills the intercellular spaces. This process is shown in **Figure 1-2**. The capillary walls are permeable to most molecules in the blood plasma, with the exception of plasma proteins, which are too large to pass through capillaries readily. Therefore, large amounts of fluid and its dissolved con stituents _diffuse_ back and forth between the blood and the tissue spaces, as shown by the arrows in **Figure 1-2**.
This process of diffusion is caused by kinetic motion of the molecules in the plasma and the interstitial fluid.

That is, the fluid and dissolved molecules are continually moving and bouncing in all directions in the plasma and fluid in the intercellular spaces, as well as through capil lary pores. Few cells are located more than 50 microm eters from a capillary, which ensures diffusion of almost any substance from the capillary to the cell within a few seconds. Thus, the extracellular fluid everywhere in the body—both that of the plasma and that of the interstitial fluid—is continually being mixed, thereby maintaining homogeneity of extracellular fluid throughout the body.
ORIGIN OF NUTRIENTS IN THE EXTRACELLULAR FLUID

**Figure 1-1** shows that each time blood passes through the body, it also flows through the lungs. The blood picks up _oxygen_ in alveoli, thus acquiring the oxygen needed by cells. The membrane between the alveoli and the lumen of the pulmonary capillaries, the _alveolar membrane,_ is only 0.4 to 2.0 micrometers thick, and oxygen rapidly diffuses by molecular motion through this membrane into the blood.

A large portion of the blood pumped by the heart also passes through the walls of the gastrointes tinal tract. Here different dissolved nutrients, including _car bohydrates, fatty acids,_ and _amino acids,_ are absorbed from ingested food into the extracellular fluid of the blood.

Not all substances absorbed from the gastrointestinal tract can be used in their absorbed form by the cells. The liver changes the chemical compositions of many of these substances to more usable forms, and other tissues of the body—fat cells, gastrointestinal mu cosa, kidneys, and endocrine glands—help modify the absorbed substances or store them until they are needed. The liver also eliminates certain waste products produced in the body and toxic substances that are ingested.

full.text: How does the musculoskeletal system contribute to homeostasis? The answer is obvious and simple. Were it not for the muscles, the body could not move to obtain the foods required for nutrition. The musculoskeletal system also provides motility for protec tion against adverse surroundings, without which the en tire body, along with its homeostatic mechanisms, could be destroyed.
REMOVAL OF METABOLIC END PRODUCTS

At the same time that blood picks up oxygen in the lungs, _carbon di oxide_ is released from the blood into lung alveoli; the res piratory movement of air into and out of the lungs carries carbon dioxide to the atmosphere. Carbon dioxide is the most abundant of all the metabolism products.
full.lead: Removal of Carbon Dioxide by the Lungs.

full.text: Passage of blood through the kidneys removes most of the other substances from the plasma besides car bon dioxide that are not needed by cells. These substanc es include different end products of cellular metabolism, such as urea and uric acid; they also include excesses of ions and water from the food that accumulate in the ex tracellular fluid.

The kidneys perform their function first by filtering large quantities of plasma through the glomerular capil laries into the tubules and then reabsorbing into the blood substances needed by the body, such as glucose, amino acids, appropriate amounts of water, and many of the ions. Most of the other substances that are not needed by the body, especially metabolic waste products such as urea and creatinine, are reabsorbed poorly and pass through the renal tubules into the urine.
Undigested material that enters the gastrointestinal tract and some waste products of me tabolism are eliminated in the feces.
Among the many functions of the liver is detoxifi cation or removal of ingested drugs and chemicals. The liver secretes many of these wastes into the bile to be eventually eliminated in the feces.
REGULATION OF BODY FUNCTIONS

The nervous system is composed of three major parts—the _sensory input portion,_ the _central nervous system_ (or _integrative portion_), and the _motor out put portion._ Sensory receptors detect the state of the body and its surroundings. For example, receptors in the skin alert us whenever an object touches the skin. The eyes are sensory organs that give us a visual image of the sur rounding area. The ears are also sensory organs. The cen tral nervous system is composed of the brain and spinal cord. The brain stores information, generates thoughts, creates ambition, and determines reactions that the body performs in response to the sensations. Appropriate sig nals are then transmitted through the motor output por tion of the nervous system to carry out one’s desires.

An important segment of the nervous system is called the _autonomic system._ It operates at a subconscious level and controls many functions of internal organs, including the level of pumping activity by the heart, movements of the gastrointestinal tract, and secretion by many of the body’s glands.

Located in the body are _endocrine glands,_ organs and tissues that secrete chemical sub stances called _hormones._ Hormones are transported in the extracellular fluid to other parts of the body to help regulate cellular function. For example, _thyroid hormone_ increases the rates of most chemical reactions in all cells, thus helping set the tempo of bodily activity. _Insulin_ con trols glucose metabolism, _adrenocortical hormones_ con trol sodium and potassium ions and protein metabolism, and _parathyroid hormone_ controls bone calcium and phosphate. Thus, the hormones provide a regulatory sys tem that complements the nervous system. The nervous system controls many muscular and secretory activities of the body, whereas the hormonal system regulates many metabolic functions. The nervous and hormonal systems normally work together in a coordinated manner to con trol essentially all the organ systems of the body.
PROTECTION OF THE BODY

The immune system includes white blood cells, tissue cells derived from white blood cells, the thymus, lymph nodes, and lymph vessels that protect the body from pathogens such as bacteria, viruses, parasites, and fungi. The immune system provides a mechanism for the body to carry out the following: (1) distinguish its own cells from harmful foreign cells and substances; and (2) destroy the invader by _phagocytosis_ or by producing _sensi tized lymphocytes_ or specialized proteins (e.g., _antibodies_) that destroy or neutralize the invader.

The skin and its various ap pendages (including the hair, nails, glands, and other structures) cover, cushion, and protect the deeper tissues and organs of the body and generally provide a bound ary between the body’s internal environment and the out side world. The integumentary system is also important for temperature regulation and excretion of wastes, and it provides a sensory interface between the body and the external environment. The skin generally comprises about 12% to 15% of body weight.

Although reproduction is sometimes not considered a homeostatic function, it helps maintain homeostasis by generating new beings to take the place of those that are dying. This may sound like a permissive usage of the term _homeostasis,_ but it illustrates that in the final analysis, essentially all body structures are organized to help main tain the automaticity and continuity of life.
CONTROL SYSTEMS OF THE BODY

The human body has thousands of control systems. Some of the most intricate of these systems are genetic control systems that operate in all cells to help regulate intracel lular and extracellular functions. This subject is discussed in Chapter 3.

Many other control systems operate _within the organs_ to regulate functions of the individual parts of the organs; others operate throughout the entire body _to control the interrelationships between the organs._ For example, the respiratory system, operating in association with the nervous system, regulates the concentration of carbon dioxide in the extracellular fluid. The liver and pancreas control glucose concentration in the extracellular fluid, and the kidneys regulate concentrations of hydrogen, sodium, potassium, phosphate, and other ions in the extracellular fluid.
EXAMPLES OF CONTROL MECHANISMS

Because oxygen is one of the major substances required for chemical reac tions in cells, the body has a special control mechanism to maintain an almost exact and constant oxygen concentra tion in the extracellular fluid. This mechanism depends principally on the chemical characteristics of _hemoglobin,_ which is present in red blood cells. Hemoglobin com bines with oxygen as the blood passes through the lungs. Then, as the blood passes through the tissue capillaries, hemoglobin, because of its own strong chemical affinity for oxygen, does not release oxygen into the tissue fluid if too much oxygen is already there. However, if oxygen concentration in the tissue fluid is too low, sufficient oxy gen is released to re-establish an adequate concentration. Thus, regulation of oxygen concentration in the tissues relies to a great extent on the chemical characteristics of hemoglobin. This regulation is called the _oxygen-buffering function of hemoglobin._
full.lead: Regulation of Oxygen and Carbon Dioxide Concentrations in the Extracellular Fluid.

full.text: Carbon dioxide concentration in the extracellular fluid is regulated in a much different way. Carbon dioxide is a major end product of oxidative reactions in cells. If all the carbon dioxide formed in the cells continued to accumu late in the tissue fluids, all energy-giving reactions of the cells would cease. Fortunately, a higher than normal car bon dioxide concentration in the blood _excites the respira tory center,_ causing a person to breathe rapidly and deeply. This deep rapid breathing increases expiration of carbon dioxide and, therefore, removes excess carbon dioxide from the blood and tissue fluids. This process continues until the concentration returns to normal.

Several systems contribute to arterial blood pressure regulation. One of these, the _baroreceptor system,_ is an excellent example of a rapidly acting control mechanism (**Figure 1-3**). In the walls of the bifurcation region of the carotid arteries in the neck, and also in the arch of the aorta in the thorax, are many nerve receptors called _baroreceptors_ that are stimulated by stretch of the arterial wall. When arterial pressure rises too high, the baroreceptors send barrages of nerve impulses to the medulla of the brain. Here, these impulses inhibit the _vasomotor center,_ which in turn de creases the number of impulses transmitted from the vasomotor center through the sympathetic nervous sys tem to the heart and blood vessels. Lack of these impulses causes diminished pumping activity by the heart and dila tion of peripheral blood vessels, allowing increased blood flow through the vessels. Both these effects decrease the arterial pressure, moving it back toward normal.

Conversely, a decrease in arterial pressure below nor mal relaxes the stretch receptors, allowing the vasomotor center to become more active than usual, thereby causing vasoconstriction and increased heart pumping. The initial decrease in arterial pressure thus initiates negative feed back mechanisms that raise arterial pressure back toward normal.
Normal Ranges and Physical Characteristics of Important Extracellular Fluid Constituents

**Table 1-1** lists some important constituents and physical characteristics of extracellular fluid, along with their nor mal values, normal ranges, and maximum limits without causing death. Note the narrowness of the normal range for each one. Values outside these ranges are often caused by illness, injury, or major environmental challenges.

Most important are the limits beyond which abnor malities can cause death. For example, an increase in the body temperature of only 11°F (7°C) above normal can lead to a vicious cycle of increasing cellular metabolism that destroys the cells. Note also the narrow range for acid–base balance in the body, with a normal pH value of 7.4 and lethal values only about 0.5 on either side of normal. Whenever the potassium ion concentration decreases to less than one-third normal, paralysis may result from the inability of the nerves to carry signals. Alternatively, if potassium ion concentration increases to two or more times normal, the heart muscle is likely to be severely depressed. Also, when the calcium ion concentration falls below about one-half normal, a per son is likely to experience tetanic contraction of muscles throughout the body because of the spontaneous genera tion of excess nerve impulses in peripheral nerves. When the glucose concentration falls below one-half normal, a person frequently exhibits extreme mental irritability and sometimes even has convulsions.

These examples should give one an appreciation for the necessity of the vast numbers of control systems that keep the body operating in health. In the absence of any one of these controls, serious body malfunction or death can result.
CHARACTERISTICS OF CONTROL SYSTEMS
The aforementioned examples of homeostatic control mechanisms are only a few of the many thousands in the body, all of which have some common characteristics, as explained in this section.
Negative Feedback Nature of Most Control Systems

Most control systems of the body act by _negative feed back,_ which can be explained by reviewing some of the homeostatic control systems mentioned previously. In the regulation of carbon dioxide concentration, a high concentration of carbon dioxide in the extracellular fluid increases pulmonary ventilation. This, in turn, decreases the extracellular fluid carbon dioxide concentration because the lungs expire greater amounts of carbon diox ide from the body. Thus, the high concentration of carbon dioxide initiates events that decrease the concentration toward normal, which is _negative_ to the initiating stimu lus. Conversely, a carbon dioxide concentration that falls too low results in feedback to increase the concentration. This response is also negative to the initiating stimulus.

In the arterial pressure–regulating mechanisms, a high pressure causes a series of reactions that promote reduced pressure, or a low pressure causes a series of reactions that promote increased pressure. In both cases, these effects are negative with respect to the initiating stimulus.

Therefore, in general, if some factor becomes exces sive or deficient, a control system initiates _negative feed back,_ which consists of a series of changes that return the factor toward a certain mean value, thus maintaining homeostasis.

The degree of effectiveness with which a control system maintains constant condi tions is determined by the _gain_ of negative feedback. For example, let us assume that a large volume of blood is transfused into a person whose baroreceptor pressure control system is not functioning, and the arterial pres sure rises from the normal level of 100 mm Hg up to 175 mm Hg. Then, let us assume that the same volume of blood is injected into the same person when the barore ceptor system is functioning, and this time the pressure increases by only 25 mm Hg. Thus, the feedback control system has caused a “correction” of −50 mm Hg, from 175 mm Hg to 125 mm Hg. There remains an increase in pressure of +25 mm Hg, called the “error,” which means that the control system is not 100% effective in preventing change. The gain of the system is then calculated by using the following formula:

Error Thus, in the baroreceptor system example, the correc tion is −50 mm Hg, and the error persisting is +25 mm Hg. Therefore, the gain of the person’s baroreceptor system for control of arterial pressure is −50 divided by +25, or −2. That is, a disturbance that increases or decreases the arterial pressure does so only one-third as much as would occur if this control system were not present.

The gains of some other physiological control systems are much greater than that of the baroreceptor system. For example, the gain of the system controlling internal body temperature when a person is exposed to moder ately cold weather is about −33. Therefore, one can see that the temperature control system is much more effec tive than the baroreceptor pressure control system.
Positive Feedback May Cause Vicious Cycles and Death

Why do most control systems of the body operate by negative feedback rather than by positive feedback? If one considers the nature of positive feedback, it is obvi ous that positive feedback leads to instability rather than stability and, in some cases, can cause death.

**Figure 1-4** shows an example in which death can ensue from positive feedback. This figure depicts the pumping effectiveness of the heart, showing the heart of a healthy human pumping about 5 liters of blood per minute. If the person suddenly bleeds a total of 2 liters, the amount of blood in the body is decreased to such a low level that not enough blood is available for the heart to pump effec tively. As a result, the arterial pressure falls, and the flow of blood to the heart muscle through the coronary ves sels diminishes. This scenario results in weakening of the heart, further diminished pumping, a further decrease in coronary blood flow, and still more weakness of the heart; the cycle repeats itself again and again until death occurs. Note that each cycle in the feedback results in further weakening of the heart. In other words, the initi ating stimulus causes more of the same, which is _positive feedback._

Positive feedback is sometimes known as a “vicious cycle,” but a mild degree of positive feedback can be overcome by the negative feedback control mechanisms of the body, and the vicious cycle then fails to develop. For example, if the person in the aforementioned example bleeds only 1 liter instead of 2 liters, the normal negative feedback mechanisms for controlling cardiac output and arterial pressure can counterbalance the positive feedback and the person can recover, as shown by the dashed curve of **Figure 1-4**.

The body sometimes uses positive feedback to its advantage. Blood clotting is an example of a valuable use of positive feed back. When a blood vessel is ruptured, and a clot begins to form, multiple enzymes called _clotting factors_ are activated within the clot. Some of these enzymes act on other inac tivated enzymes of the immediately adjacent blood, thus causing more blood clotting. This process continues until the hole in the vessel is plugged and bleeding no longer occurs. On occasion, this mechanism can get out of hand and cause formation of unwanted clots. In fact, this is what initiates most acute heart attacks, which can be caused by a clot beginning on the inside surface of an atherosclerotic plaque in a coronary artery and then growing until the ar tery is blocked.
full.lead: Positive Feedback Can Sometimes Be Useful.

full.text: Childbirth is another situation in which positive feed back is valuable. When uterine contractions become strong enough for the baby’s head to begin pushing through the cervix, stretching of the cervix sends signals through the uterine muscle back to the body of the uterus, causing even more powerful contractions. Thus, the uter ine contractions stretch the cervix, and cervical stretch causes stronger contractions. When this process becomes powerful enough, the baby is born. If they are not pow erful enough, the contractions usually die out, and a few days pass before they begin again.

Another important use of positive feedback is for the generation of nerve signals. Stimulation of the mem brane of a nerve fiber causes slight leakage of sodium ions through sodium channels in the nerve membrane to the fiber’s interior. The sodium ions entering the fiber then change the membrane potential, which, in turn, causes more opening of channels, more change of potential, still more opening of channels, and so forth. Thus, a slight leak becomes an explosion of sodium entering the interior of the nerve fiber, which creates the nerve action potential. This action potential, in turn, causes electrical current to flow along the outside and inside of the fiber and initiates additional action potentials. This process continues until the nerve signal goes all the way to the end of the fiber.

In each case in which positive feedback is useful, the positive feedback is part of an overall negative feedback process. For example, in the case of blood clotting, the positive feedback clotting process is a negative feedback process for the maintenance of normal blood volume. Also, the positive feedback that causes nerve signals allows the nerves to participate in thousands of negative feedback nervous control systems.
More Complex Types of Control Systems—Feed-Forward and Adaptive Control

Later in this text, when we study the nervous system, we shall see that this system contains great numbers of inter connected control mechanisms. Some are simple feedback systems similar to those already discussed. Many are not. For example, some movements of the body occur so rap idly that there is not enough time for nerve signals to travel from the peripheral parts of the body all the way to the brain and then back to the periphery again to control the movement. Therefore, the brain uses a mechanism called _feed-forward control_ to cause required muscle contrac tions. Sensory nerve signals from the moving parts apprise the brain about whether the movement is performed cor rectly. If not, the brain corrects the feed-forward signals that it sends to the muscles the _next_ time the movement is required. Then, if still further correction is necessary, this process will be performed again for subsequent move ments. This process is called _adaptive control._ Adaptive control, in a sense, is delayed negative feedback.

Thus, one can see how complex the feedback control systems of the body can be. A person’s life depends on all of them. Therefore, much of this text is devoted to dis cussing these life-giving mechanisms.
PHYSIOLOGICAL VARIABILITY

Although some physiological variables, such as plasma concentrations of potassium, calcium, and hydrogen ions, are tightly regulated, others, such as body weight and adiposity, show wide variation among different indi viduals and even in the same individual at different stages of life. Blood pressure, cardiac pumping, metabolic rate, nervous system activity, hormones, and other physi ological variables change throughout the day as we move about and engage in normal daily activities. Therefore, when we discuss “normal” values, it is with the under standing that many of the body’s control systems are con stantly reacting to perturbations, and that variability may exist among different individuals, depending on body weight and height, diet, age, sex, environment, genetics, and other factors.

For simplicity, discussion of physiological functions often focuses on the “average” 70-kg young, lean male. However, the American male no longer weighs an aver age of 70 kg; he now weighs over 88 kg, and the average American female weighs over 76 kg, more than the aver age man in the 1960s. Body weight has also increased sub stantially in most other industrialized countries during the past 40 to 50 years.

Except for reproductive and hormonal functions, many other physiological functions and normal values are often discussed in terms of male physiology. However, there are clearly differences in male and female physiology beyond the obvious differences that relate to reproduc tion. These differences can have important consequences for understanding normal physiology as well as for treat ment of diseases.

Age-related and ethnic or racial differences in physiol ogy also have important influences on body composition, physiological control systems, and pathophysiology of diseases. For example, in a lean young male the total body water is about 60% of body weight. As a person grows and ages, this percentage gradually decreases, partly because aging is usually associated with declining skeletal muscle mass and increasing fat mass. Aging may also cause a decline in the function and effectiveness of some organs and physiological control systems.
These sources of physiological variability—sex differ ences, aging, ethnic, and racial—are complex but impor tant considerations when discussing normal physiology and the pathophysiology of diseases.
SUMMARY—AUTOMATICITY OF THE BODY

The main purpose of this chapter has been to discuss briefly the overall organization of the body and the means whereby the different parts of the body operate in har mony. To summarize, the body is actually a _social order of about 35 to 40 trillion cells_ organized into different func tional structures, some of which are called _organs._ Each functional structure contributes its share to the mainte nance of homeostasis in the extracellular fluid, which is called the _internal environment._ As long as normal con ditions are maintained in this internal environment, the cells of the body continue to live and function properly. Each cell benefits from homeostasis and, in turn, each cell contributes its share toward the maintenance of homeostasis. This reciprocal interplay provides continu ous automaticity of the body until one or more functional systems lose their ability to contribute their share of func tion. When this happens, all the cells of the body suffer. Extreme dysfunction leads to death; moderate dysfunc tion leads to sickness.

ch01-f12.lead: Hujayradan taşqari va hujayra içidagi suyuqliklarning farqlari.

ch01-f13.text: Hujayra içidagi suyuqlikda hujayradan taşqari suyuqlikdagi natriy va xlor ionlari örniga köp miqdorda kaliy, magniy va fosfat ionlari bor. Ionlarni hujayra membranalari orqali taşuvçi maxsus mexanizmlar hujayradan taşqari va hujayra içidagi suyuqliklar örtasidagi ion konsentratsiyalari farqini saqlab turadi. Bu taşiş jarayonlari 4-bobda muhokama qilinadi.

ch01-f14.text: Gomeostaz — içki muhitning deyarli doimiyligini saqlaş

ch01-f15.text: 1929-yilda amerikalik fiziolog Uolter Kennon (1871–1945) _içki muhitda deyarli doimiy şaroitlarning saqlanişini_ ifodalaş uçun _gomeostaz_ atamasini kiritdi. Mohiyatan organizmning barça a’zolari va töqimalari ana şu nisbatan doimiy şaroitlarni saqlaşga yordam beradigan funksiyalarni bajaradi. Masalan, öpkalar hujayralar sarflagan kislorodni töldiriş uçun hujayradan taşqari suyuqlikni kislorod bilan ta’minlaydi, buyraklar ion konsentratsiyalarini doimiy saqlaydi, me’da-içak tizimi esa ozuqa moddalarini yetkazib beriş bilan birga organizmdan çiqindilarni çiqaradi.

ch01-f16.text: Organizmdagi turli ionlar, ozuqa moddalari, çiqindi mahsulotlar va boşqa tarkibiy qismlar odatda qat’iy belgilangan qiymatlarda emas, balki muayyan qiymatlar oraliğida boşqariladi. Organizmning ba’zi tarkibiy qismlari uçun bu oraliq nihoyatda tor. Masalan, qondagi vodorod ionlari konsentratsiyasining özgarişlari odatda 5 _nanomol/L_ (0,000000005 mol/L) dan kam böladi. Qondagi natriy konsentratsiyasi ham qat’iy boşqariladi: natriy iste’moli katta miqdorda özgarganda ham u odatda litriga atigi bir neça _millimol_ ga özgaradi, biroq natriy konsentratsiyasining bu özgarişlari vodorod ionlarinikidan kamida 1 million marta katta.

ch01-f17.text: Atrof-muhitning keng özgarişlari hamda jarohat va kasalliklar keltirib çiqaradigan sinovlarga qaramay, natriy va vodorod ionlari, şuningdek, organizmdagi boşqa ionlar, ozuqa moddalari va moddalarning aksariyati konsentratsiyalarini hujayralar, töqimalar va a’zolarning me’yoriy funksiyalarini bajarişiga imkon beradigan darajada saqlab turuvçi kuçli boşqaruv tizimlari mavjud.

ch01-f18.text: Uşbu darslikning katta qismi har bir a’zo yoki töqimaning gomeostazga qanday hissa qöşişiga bağişlangan. Organizmning me’yoriy funksiyalari hujayralar, töqimalar, a’zolar hamda birgalikda gomeostaz va soğliqni ta’minlovçi köplab nerv, gormonal va mahalliy boşqaruv tizimlarining integratsiyalaşgan faoliyatini talab qiladi.

ch01-f19.text: _Kasallik_ köpinça gomeostaz buzilgan holat deb qaraladi. Biroq kasallik mavjud bölganda ham gomeostatik mexanizmlar işlaşda davom etadi va köplab kompensatsiyalar orqali hayotiy muhim funksiyalarni saqlab turadi. Ba’zi hollarda bu kompensatsiyalar organizm funksiyalarining me’yoriy oraliqdan katta oğişiga olib kelişi mumkin; bunda kasallikning birlamçi sababini kompensator javoblardan ajratiş qiyinlaşadi. Masalan, buyraklarning tuz va suvni çiqariş qobiliyatini buzadigan kasalliklar yuqori arterial bosimga olib kelişi mumkin; u dastlab çiqarişni me’yorga qaytarişga yordam beradi, natijada iste’mol va buyrak orqali çiqariş örtasidagi muvozanat saqlanadi. Bu muvozanat hayotni saqlaş uçun zarur, biroq uzoq vaqt davomida yuqori arterial bosim turli a’zolarni, jumladan buyraklarni ham şikastlaşi mumkin; bu esa arterial bosimning yanada köproq oşişiga va buyraklarning yanada kuçliroq şikastlanişiga sabab böladi. Şunday qilib, jarohat, kasallik yoki organizmga atrof-muhitning kuçli ta’siridan keyin yuzaga keladigan gomeostatik kompensatsiyalar hayotiy muhim funksiyalarni saqlaş uçun zarur bölgan, ammo uzoq muddatda organizm funksiyalarining qöşimça buzilişlariga hissa qöşadigan murosani ifodalaşi mumkin. _Patofiziologiya_ fani turli fiziologik jarayonlar kasallik yoki jarohatda qanday özgarişini tuşuntirişga intiladi.

ch01-f20.text: Uşbu bobda organizmning turli funksional tizimlari va ularning gomeostazga qöşadigan hissasi qisqaça bayon qilinadi. Söngra funksional tizimlarning bir-birini qöllab-quvvatlagan holda işlaşiga imkon beruvçi organizm boşqaruv tizimlarining asosiy nazariyasini qisqaça muhokama qilamiz.

ch01-f21.text: Hujayradan taşqari suyuqlikni taşuvçi va aralaştiruvçi tizim — qon aylaniş tizimi

ch01-f22.text: Hujayradan taşqari suyuqlik organizm böylab ikki bosqiçda taşiladi. Birinçi bosqiç — qonning qon tomirlari orqali organizm böylab harakati. Ikkinçisi — suyuqlikning qon kapillyarlari va töqima hujayralari orasidagi _hujayralararo böşliqlar_ örtasidagi harakati.

ch01-f23.text: **Rasm 1-1** da qon aylanişining umumiy sxemasi körsatilgan. Qon aylanişidagi butun qon tinç holatda butun aylaniş yölini örtaça har daqiqada bir marta, odam juda faol bölganda esa daqiqasiga olti martagaça bosib ötadi.

ch01-f25.text: Qon kapillyarlardan ötayotganda qonning plazma qismi bilan hujayralararo böşliqlarni töldiruvçi interstitsial suyuqlik örtasida hujayradan taşqari suyuqlikning uzluksiz almaşinuvi sodir böladi. Bu jarayon **Rasm 1-2** da körsatilgan. Kapillyar devorlari qon plazmasidagi molekulalarning aksariyatini ötkazadi; bundan plazma oqsillari mustasno, çunki ular kapillyarlardan oson ötiş uçun juda yirik. Şu sababli, **Rasm 1-2** dagi strelkalar bilan körsatilganidek, köp miqdordagi suyuqlik va unda erigan tarkibiy qismlar qon bilan töqima böşliqlari örtasida u yoqdan bu yoqqa _diffuziyalanadi_.

ch01-f27.text: Bu diffuziya jarayoni plazma va interstitsial suyuqlikdagi molekulalarning kinetik harakati tufayli yuzaga keladi.

ch01-f28.text: Ya’ni suyuqlik va unda erigan molekulalar plazmada va hujayralararo böşliqlardagi suyuqlikda, şuningdek, kapillyar teşikçalari orqali doimiy ravişda harakatlanib, barça yönalişlarda töqnaşib turadi. Kapillyardan 50 mikrometrdan uzoqroqda joylaşgan hujayralar juda kam; bu deyarli har qanday moddaning kapillyardan hujayragaça bir neça sekund içida diffuziyalanişini ta’minlaydi. Şunday qilib, organizmning hamma joyidagi hujayradan taşqari suyuqlik — plazma ham, interstitsial suyuqlik ham — uzluksiz aralaşib turadi va şu tufayli butun organizm böylab hujayradan taşqari suyuqlikning bir jinsliligi saqlanadi.

ch01-f29.text: Hujayradan taşqari suyuqlikdagi ozuqa moddalarining manbalari

ch01-f30.text: **Rasm 1-1** dan körinib turibdiki, qon har safar organizm böylab aylanganda öpkadan ham ötadi. Qon alveolalarda _kislorodni_ biriktirib oladi va şu tariqa hujayralarga zarur bölgan kislorodga ega böladi. Alveolalar bilan öpka kapillyarlari böşliği örtasidagi membrana — _alveolyar membrana_ — atigi 0,4–2,0 mikrometr qalinlikda bölib, kislorod molekulyar harakat orqali bu membranadan qonga tez diffuziyalanadi.

ch01-f31.text: Yurak haydaydigan qonning katta qismi me’da-içak yöli devorlaridan ham ötadi. Bu yerda iste’mol qilingan ovqatdan turli erigan ozuqa moddalari, jumladan _uglevodlar, yoğ kislotalari_ va _aminokislotalar_ qonning hujayradan taşqari suyuqligiga söriladi.

ch01-f32.text: Me’da-içak yölidan sörilgan barça moddalarni ham hujayralar sörilgan şaklida foydalana olmaydi. Jigar bu moddalarning köpçiligining kimyoviy tarkibini foydalaniş uçun qulayroq şakllarga özgartiradi, organizmning boşqa töqimalari — yoğ hujayralari, me’da-içak şilliq qavati, buyraklar va endokrin bezlar — esa sörilgan moddalarni özgartirişga yoki ular kerak bölgunça zaxirada saqlaşga yordam beradi. Jigar, şuningdek, organizmda hosil böladigan ba’zi çiqindi mahsulotlarni va iste’mol qilingan zaharli moddalarni ham çiqarib taşlaydi.
ch01-f32.lead: Jigar va asosan metabolik funksiyalarni bajaruvçi boşqa a’zolar.

ch01-f33.text: Tayanç-harakat tizimi gomeostazga qanday hissa qöşadi? Javob ravşan va oddiy. Muskullar bölmaganida organizm ovqatlaniş uçun zarur oziq-ovqatni topiş maqsadida harakatlana olmas edi. Tayanç-harakat tizimi, şuningdek, noqulay muhitdan himoyalaniş uçun harakatçanlikni ta’minlaydi; usiz butun organizm özining gomeostatik mexanizmlari bilan birga halok bölişi mumkin edi.

ch01-f35.text: Qon öpkada kislorodni biriktirib olayotgan bir paytda qondan öpka alveolalariga _karbonat angidrid_ ajraladi; havoning öpkaga kirib-çiqişidan iborat nafas harakatlari karbonat angidridni atmosferaga olib çiqadi. Karbonat angidrid moddalar almaşinuvining barça mahsulotlari orasida eng köp hosil böladiganidir.

ch01-f36.text: Qon buyraklardan ötganda plazmadan karbonat angidriddan taşqari hujayralarga kerak bölmagan boşqa moddalarning köpçiligi çiqarib taşlanadi. Bu moddalarga hujayra metabolizmining turli oxirgi mahsulotlari, masalan, moçevina va siydik kislotasi, şuningdek, ovqat bilan tuşib hujayradan taşqari suyuqlikda töplanadigan ortiqça ionlar va suv kiradi.

ch01-f37.text: Buyraklar öz funksiyasini quyidagiça bajaradi: avval katta hajmdagi plazmani koptokça kapillyarlari orqali kanalçalarga filtrlaydi, söngra organizmga kerakli moddalarni — glukoza, aminokislotalar, kerakli miqdordagi suv va köplab ionlarni — qonga qayta söradi. Organizmga kerak bölmagan boşqa moddalarning aksariyati, ayniqsa moçevina va kreatinin kabi metabolik çiqindi mahsulotlar, yomon qayta söriladi va buyrak kanalçalari orqali siydikka ötadi.

ch01-f38.text: Me’da-içak yöliga tuşgan hazm bölmagan moddalar va metabolizmning ba’zi çiqindi mahsulotlari najas bilan çiqariladi.

ch01-f39.text: Jigarning köplab funksiyalaridan biri — iste’mol qilingan dori vositalari va kimyoviy moddalarni zararsizlantiriş yoki çiqarib taşlaş. Jigar bu çiqindilarning köpini ötga ajratadi va ular oxir-oqibat najas bilan çiqariladi.

ch01-f41.text: Nerv tizimi uç asosiy qismdan iborat: _sezuvçi (afferent) qism_, _markaziy nerv tizimi_ (yoki _integrativ qism_) va _harakatlantiruvçi (efferent) qism._ Sezuvçi retseptorlar organizmning va uni örab turgan muhitning holatini aniqlaydi. Masalan, teridagi retseptorlar biror narsa teriga tegişi bilan bizni ogohlantiradi. Közlar atrofimizdagi muhitning köriş tasvirini beruvçi sezgi a’zolaridir. Quloqlar ham sezgi a’zolaridir. Markaziy nerv tizimi boş miya va orqa miyadan taşkil topgan. Boş miya axborotni saqlaydi, fikrlarni hosil qiladi, intilişlarni yuzaga keltiradi va organizm sezgilarga javoban bajaradigan reaksiyalarni belgilaydi. Söngra tegişli signallar insonning xohişlarini amalga oşiriş uçun nerv tizimining harakatlantiruvçi qismi orqali uzatiladi.

ch01-f42.text: Nerv tizimining muhim bölimi _vegetativ (avtonom) nerv tizimi_ deb ataladi. U ongsiz darajada işlaydi va içki a’zolarning köplab funksiyalarini, jumladan yurakning nasos faolligi darajasini, me’da-içak yöli harakatlarini va organizmdagi köplab bezlarning sekretsiyasini boşqaradi.

ch01-f43.text: Organizmda _endokrin bezlar_ — _gormonlar_ deb ataladigan kimyoviy moddalarni ajratuvçi a’zolar va töqimalar joylaşgan. Gormonlar hujayradan taşqari suyuqlik orqali organizmning boşqa qismlariga taşiladi va hujayra funksiyasini boşqarişga yordam beradi. Masalan, _qalqonsimon bez gormoni_ barça hujayralardagi kimyoviy reaksiyalarning köpçiligi tezligini oşiradi va şu tariqa organizm faolligi sur’atini belgilaşga yordam beradi. _Insulin_ glukoza metabolizmini boşqaradi, _buyrak usti bezi pöstloği gormonlari_ natriy va kaliy ionlari hamda oqsillar metabolizmini boşqaradi, _paratgormon_ (qalqonsimon bez oldi bezi gormoni) esa suyakdagi kalsiy va fosfatni boşqaradi. Şunday qilib, gormonlar nerv tizimini töldiruvçi boşqaruv tizimini ta’minlaydi. Nerv tizimi organizmning köplab muskul va sekretor faoliyatini boşqaradi, gormonal tizim esa köplab metabolik funksiyalarni boşqaradi. Nerv va gormonal tizimlar odatda organizmning deyarli barça a’zolar tizimlarini boşqariş uçun muvofiqlaşgan holda birgalikda işlaydi.

ch01-f45.text: Immun tizimiga oq qon hujayralari (leykotsitlar), leykotsitlardan kelib çiqqan töqima hujayralari, ayrisimon bez (timus), limfa tugunlari va limfa tomirlari kiradi; ular organizmni bakteriyalar, viruslar, parazitlar va zamburuğlar kabi patogenlardan himoya qiladi. Immun tizimi organizmga quyidagilarni amalga oşiriş mexanizmini beradi: (1) öz hujayralarini zararli begona hujayralar va moddalardan farqlaş; (2) bosqinçini _fagotsitoz_ yöli bilan yoki bosqinçini yöq qiluvçi yoki zararsizlantiruvçi _sensibilizatsiyalangan limfotsitlar_ yoxud maxsus oqsillar (masalan, _antitanalar_) hosil qiliş orqali yöq qiliş.

ch01-f46.text: Teri va uning turli hosilalari (jumladan soçlar, tirnoqlar, bezlar va boşqa tuzilmalar) organizmning çuqurroq joylaşgan töqimalari va a’zolarini qoplaydi, yumşatadi va himoya qiladi hamda umuman organizmning içki muhiti bilan taşqi dunyo örtasida çegara vazifasini ötaydi. Qoplovçi tizim, şuningdek, harorat boşqaruvi va çiqindilarni çiqariş uçun ham muhim, u organizm bilan taşqi muhit örtasida sezgi aloqasini ham ta’minlaydi. Teri odatda tana vaznining taxminan 12–15% ini taşkil qiladi.

ch01-f47.text: Köpayiş ba’zan gomeostatik funksiya deb hisoblanmasa-da, u nobud bölayotgan mavjudotlar örnini egallaydigan yangi mavjudotlarni hosil qiliş orqali gomeostazni saqlaşga yordam beradi. Bu _gomeostaz_ atamasining biroz erkin qöllanişidek tuyulişi mumkin, biroq u oxir-oqibat organizmning deyarli barça tuzilmalari hayotning avtomatikligi va uzluksizligini saqlaşga yordam beriş uçun taşkil topganini körsatadi.

ch01-f49.text: Inson organizmida minglab boşqaruv tizimlari bor. Ulardan eng murakkablari qatoriga barça hujayralarda işlaydigan va hujayra içidagi hamda hujayradan taşqari funksiyalarni boşqarişga yordam beradigan genetik boşqaruv tizimlari kiradi. Bu mavzu 3-bobda muhokama qilinadi.

ch01-f50.text: Köplab boşqa boşqaruv tizimlari a’zolarning alohida qismlari funksiyalarini boşqariş uçun _a’zolar içida_ işlaydi; boşqalari esa butun organizm böylab _a’zolar örtasidagi özaro munosabatlarni boşqariş uçun_ işlaydi. Masalan, nafas oliş tizimi nerv tizimi bilan hamkorlikda hujayradan taşqari suyuqlikdagi karbonat angidrid konsentratsiyasini boşqaradi. Jigar va me’da osti bezi hujayradan taşqari suyuqlikdagi glukoza konsentratsiyasini nazorat qiladi, buyraklar esa hujayradan taşqari suyuqlikdagi vodorod, natriy, kaliy, fosfat va boşqa ionlar konsentratsiyalarini boşqaradi.

ch01-f52.text: Kislorod hujayralardagi kimyoviy reaksiyalar uçun zarur bölgan asosiy moddalardan biri bölgani sababli, organizmda hujayradan taşqari suyuqlikda kislorod konsentratsiyasini deyarli aniq va doimiy saqlab turuvçi maxsus boşqaruv mexanizmi mavjud. Bu mexanizm asosan eritrotsitlarda böladigan _gemoglobinning_ kimyoviy xususiyatlariga boğliq. Qon öpkadan ötayotganda gemoglobin kislorod bilan birikadi. Söngra qon töqima kapillyarlaridan ötayotganda gemoglobin kislorodga kuçli kimyoviy moyilligi tufayli, agar töqima suyuqligida kislorod allaqaçon juda köp bölsa, uni töqima suyuqligiga bermaydi. Biroq töqima suyuqligida kislorod konsentratsiyasi juda past bölsa, yetarli konsentratsiyani tiklaş uçun yetarliça kislorod ajraladi. Şunday qilib, töqimalardagi kislorod konsentratsiyasining boşqarilişi köp jihatdan gemoglobinning kimyoviy xususiyatlariga tayanadi. Bu boşqaruv _gemoglobinning kislorodni buferlaş funksiyasi_ deb ataladi.
ch01-f52.lead: Hujayradan taşqari suyuqlikdagi kislorod va karbonat angidrid konsentratsiyalarining boşqarilişi.

ch01-f53.text: Hujayradan taşqari suyuqlikdagi karbonat angidrid konsentratsiyasi butunlay boşqaça yöl bilan boşqariladi. Karbonat angidrid hujayralardagi oksidlaniş reaksiyalarining asosiy oxirgi mahsulotidir. Agar hujayralarda hosil bölgan barça karbonat angidrid töqima suyuqliklarida töplanişda davom etsa, hujayralarning energiya beruvçi barça reaksiyalari töxtab qolar edi. Yaxşiyamki, qonda karbonat angidrid konsentratsiyasining me’yordan yuqori bölişi _nafas markazini qözğatadi_ va odam tez va çuqur nafas ola boşlaydi. Bu çuqur va tez nafas karbonat angidridning nafas çiqariş bilan çiqarilişini kuçaytiradi va şu sababli ortiqça karbonat angidridni qon va töqima suyuqliklaridan çiqarib taşlaydi. Bu jarayon konsentratsiya me’yorga qaytgunça davom etadi.

ch01-f54.text: Arterial bosimni boşqarişda bir neçta tizim iştirok etadi. Ulardan biri — _baroretseptor tizimi_ — tez ta’sir qiluvçi boşqaruv mexanizmining ajoyib namunasidir (**Rasm 1-3**). Böyindagi uyqu arteriyalarining ikkiga böliniş sohasi devorlarida, şuningdek, kökrak qafasidagi aorta ravoğida arteriya devorining çözilişi bilan qözğaladigan, _baroretseptorlar_ deb ataladigan köplab nerv retseptorlari joylaşgan. Arterial bosim haddan taşqari oşganda baroretseptorlar boş miyaning uzunçoq miya qismiga nerv impulslari oqimini yuboradi. Bu yerda uşbu impulslar _vazomotor markazni_ tormozlaydi; bu esa öz navbatida vazomotor markazdan simpatik nerv tizimi orqali yurak va qon tomirlariga uzatiladigan impulslar sonini kamaytiradi. Bu impulslarning kamayişi yurakning nasos faolligini susaytiradi va periferik qon tomirlarini kengaytiradi, natijada tomirlar orqali qon oqimi ortadi. Bu ikkala ta’sir arterial bosimni pasaytiradi va uni me’yorga qaytaradi.

ch01-f56.text: Aksinça, arterial bosimning me’yordan pasayişi çöziliş retseptorlarini böşaştiradi; bu vazomotor markazning odatdagidan faolroq bölişiga imkon beradi va natijada tomirlar torayadi (vazokonstriksiya), yurakning nasos faolligi esa kuçayadi. Şunday qilib, arterial bosimning dastlabki pasayişi arterial bosimni yana me’yorga kötaruvçi manfiy teskari aloqa mexanizmlarini işga tuşiradi.

ch01-f57.text: Hujayradan taşqari suyuqlikning muhim tarkibiy qismlari va fizik xususiyatlarining me’yoriy çegaralari

ch01-f58.text: **Jadval 1-1** da hujayradan taşqari suyuqlikning ba’zi muhim tarkibiy qismlari va fizik xususiyatlari, ularning me’yoriy qiymatlari, me’yoriy çegaralari va ölimga olib kelmaydigan maksimal çegaralari keltirilgan. Har biri uçun me’yoriy çegaraning naqadar tor ekaniga e’tibor bering. Bu çegaralardan taşqaridagi qiymatlar köpinça kasallik, jarohat yoki atrof-muhitning kuçli ta’siri natijasida yuzaga keladi.

ch01-f60.text: Eng muhimi — oğişlar ölimga olib kelişi mumkin bölgan çegaralardir. Masalan, tana haroratining me’yordan atigi 11°F (7°C) ga oşişi hujayra metabolizmini kuçaytirib, hujayralarni halok qiluvçi ayovsiz doiraga olib kelişi mumkin. Organizmdagi kislota–asos muvozanatining ham tor çegarasiga e’tibor bering: me’yoriy pH qiymati 7,4 ga teng, ölimga olib keluvçi qiymatlar esa me’yordan har ikki tomonga atigi taxminan 0,5 ga farq qiladi. Kaliy ionlari konsentratsiyasi me’yorning uçdan biridan kamroqqaça pasayganda, nervlarning signal ötkaza olmasligi sababli falaj yuzaga kelişi mumkin. Aksinça, kaliy ionlari konsentratsiyasi me’yordan ikki va undan köp marta oşsa, yurak muskuli faoliyati keskin susayişi ehtimoli katta. Şuningdek, kalsiy ionlari konsentratsiyasi me’yorning taxminan yarmidan pastga tuşganda, periferik nervlarda ortiqça nerv impulslarining öz-özidan hosil bölişi tufayli odamda butun tana muskullarining tetanik qisqarişi kuzatilişi mumkin. Glukoza konsentratsiyasi me’yorning yarmidan pastga tuşganda odamda köpinça kuçli ruhiy qözğaluvçanlik namoyon böladi, ba’zan hatto tutqanoq (talvasalar) ham yuzaga keladi.

ch01-f61.text: Bu misollar organizmning soğlom işlaşini ta’minlovçi juda köp sonli boşqaruv tizimlari naqadar zarur ekanini anglaşga yordam berişi kerak. Uşbu boşqaruvlardan birortasi bölmasa, organizm faoliyatining jiddiy buzilişi yoki ölim yuz berişi mumkin.

ch01-f63.text: Gomeostatik boşqaruv mexanizmlarining yuqorida keltirilgan misollari organizmdagi minglab mexanizmlarning bir qançasigina xolos; uşbu bölimda tuşuntirilganidek, ularning barçasi ba’zi umumiy xususiyatlarga ega.

ch01-f64.text: Köpçilik boşqaruv tizimlarining manfiy teskari aloqa tabiati

ch01-f65.text: Organizmning köpçilik boşqaruv tizimlari _manfiy teskari aloqa_ (negative feedback) orqali işlaydi; buni yuqorida tilga olingan ba’zi gomeostatik boşqaruv tizimlarini körib çiqiş orqali tuşuntiriş mumkin. Karbonat angidrid konsentratsiyasini boşqarişda hujayradan taşqari suyuqlikdagi karbonat angidridning yuqori konsentratsiyasi öpka ventilyatsiyasini kuçaytiradi. Bu esa öz navbatida hujayradan taşqari suyuqlikdagi karbonat angidrid konsentratsiyasini pasaytiradi, çunki öpkalar organizmdan köproq karbonat angidridni çiqaradi. Şunday qilib, karbonat angidridning yuqori konsentratsiyasi konsentratsiyani me’yor tomon pasaytiradigan hodisalarni işga tuşiradi; bu dastlabki qözğatuvçi ta’sirga nisbatan _manfiydir_. Aksinça, karbonat angidrid konsentratsiyasi haddan taşqari pasayib ketsa, teskari aloqa konsentratsiyani oşirişga olib keladi. Bu javob ham dastlabki qözğatuvçi ta’sirga nisbatan manfiydir.

ch01-f66.text: Arterial bosimni boşqaruvçi mexanizmlarda yuqori bosim bosimni pasaytiruvçi bir qator reaksiyalarni, past bosim esa bosimni oşiruvçi bir qator reaksiyalarni keltirib çiqaradi. Har ikki holatda ham bu ta’sirlar dastlabki qözğatuvçi ta’sirga nisbatan manfiydir.

ch01-f67.text: Demak, umuman olganda, agar biror omil haddan taşqari köpayib yoki kamayib ketsa, boşqaruv tizimi _manfiy teskari aloqani_ işga tuşiradi; u omilni muayyan örtaça qiymat tomon qaytaruvçi bir qator özgarişlardan iborat bölib, şu tariqa gomeostazni saqlaydi.

ch01-f68.text: Boşqaruv tizimining doimiy şaroitlarni saqlaşdagi samaradorlik darajasi manfiy teskari aloqaning _kuçaytiriş koeffitsiyenti_ (gain) bilan belgilanadi. Masalan, faraz qilaylik, baroretseptorli bosim boşqaruv tizimi işlamayotgan odamga katta hajmda qon quyildi va arterial bosim me’yoriy 100 mm Hg darajasidan 175 mm Hg gaça kötarildi. Söngra faraz qilaylik, xuddi şu hajmdagi qon baroretseptor tizimi işlab turgan öşa odamga yuborildi va bu safar bosim atigi 25 mm Hg ga oşdi. Şunday qilib, teskari aloqali boşqaruv tizimi bosimni 175 mm Hg dan 125 mm Hg gaça, ya’ni −50 mm Hg ga “tuzatgan” (korreksiya qilgan). Bosimning +25 mm Hg ga teng ortişi saqlanib qoladi; u “xato” deb ataladi va boşqaruv tizimi özgarişning oldini olişda 100% samarali emasligini bildiradi. Şunda tizimning kuçaytiriş koeffitsiyenti quyidagi formula böyiça hisoblanadi:

ch01-f69.text: Kuçaytiriş koeffitsiyenti = Korreksiya / Xato. Şunday qilib, baroretseptor tizimi misolida korreksiya −50 mm Hg ga, saqlanib qolgan xato esa +25 mm Hg ga teng. Demak, odamning arterial bosimni boşqaruvçi baroretseptor tizimining kuçaytiriş koeffitsiyenti −50 ning +25 ga bölinmasiga, ya’ni −2 ga teng. Boşqaça aytganda, arterial bosimni oşiruvçi yoki pasaytiruvçi buzuvçi ta’sir bu boşqaruv tizimi bölmaganda yuz beradigan özgarişning atigi uçdan bir qismiçalik özgariş keltirib çiqaradi.

ch01-f70.text: Ba’zi boşqa fiziologik boşqaruv tizimlarining kuçaytiriş koeffitsiyentlari baroretseptor tiziminikidan ança katta. Masalan, odam örtaça sovuq havo ta’siriga uçraganda tananing içki haroratini boşqaruvçi tizimning kuçaytiriş koeffitsiyenti taxminan −33 ga teng. Bundan körinib turibdiki, harorat boşqaruv tizimi baroretseptorli bosim boşqaruv tizimiga qaraganda ança samaraliroq.

ch01-f71.text: Musbat teskari aloqa ayovsiz doiralar va ölimga sabab bölişi mumkin

ch01-f72.text: Nega organizmning köpçilik boşqaruv tizimlari musbat teskari aloqa bilan emas, balki manfiy teskari aloqa bilan işlaydi? Musbat teskari aloqaning tabiatini körib çiqsak, u barqarorlikka emas, balki beqarorlikka olib kelişi va ba’zi hollarda ölimga sabab bölişi mumkinligi ravşan böladi.

ch01-f73.text: **Rasm 1-4** da musbat teskari aloqa natijasida ölim yuz berişi mumkin bölgan misol körsatilgan. Bu rasmda yurakning nasos samaradorligi tasvirlangan: soğlom odamning yuragi daqiqasiga taxminan 5 litr qon haydaydi. Agar odam tösatdan jami 2 litr qon yöqotsa, organizmdagi qon miqdori şunçalik kamayadiki, yurak samarali haydaşi uçun yetarli qon qolmaydi. Natijada arterial bosim pasayadi va koronar tomirlar orqali yurak muskuliga keladigan qon oqimi kamayadi. Bu holat yurakning zaiflaşişiga, nasos faolligining yanada pasayişiga, koronar qon oqimining yanada kamayişiga va yurakning yana ham köproq zaiflaşişiga olib keladi; bu doira ölim yuz bergunça qayta-qayta takrorlanadi. E’tibor bering, teskari aloqaning har bir aylanişi yurakni yanada zaiflaştiradi. Boşqaça aytganda, dastlabki qözğatuvçi ta’sir öziga öxşaş ta’sirni yanada kuçaytiradi; bu _musbat teskari aloqadir._

ch01-f75.text: Musbat teskari aloqa ba’zan “ayovsiz doira” deb ataladi, biroq musbat teskari aloqaning yengil darajasini organizmning manfiy teskari aloqali boşqaruv mexanizmlari bartaraf etişi mumkin va bunda ayovsiz doira rivojlanmaydi. Masalan, yuqoridagi misoldagi odam 2 litr örniga atigi 1 litr qon yöqotsa, yurakning daqiqalik hajmi va arterial bosimni boşqaruvçi me’yoriy manfiy teskari aloqa mexanizmlari musbat teskari aloqani muvozanatlaşi mumkin va odam, **Rasm 1-4** dagi uzuq çiziqli egri çiziqda körsatilganidek, tuzalib ketadi.

ch01-f76.text: Organizm ba’zan musbat teskari aloqadan öz foydasiga foydalanadi. Qon ivişi musbat teskari aloqadan foydali tarzda foydalanişning namunasidir. Qon tomiri yorilib, laxta hosil böla boşlaganda, laxta içida _iviş omillari_ deb ataladigan köplab fermentlar faollaşadi. Bu fermentlarning ba’zilari bevosita qöşni qondagi boşqa nofaol fermentlarga ta’sir qiladi va şu bilan qonning yanada köproq ivişiga sabab böladi. Bu jarayon tomirdagi teşik berkilib, qon ketiş töxtagunça davom etadi. Ba’zan bu mexanizm nazoratdan çiqib, keraksiz laxtalar hosil bölişiga sabab bölişi mumkin. Aslida ötkir yurak xurujlarining aksariyati aynan şu tarzda boşlanadi: ular koronar arteriyadagi aterosklerotik pilakçaning içki yuzasida boşlanib, arteriya berkilgunça ösib boradigan laxta tufayli yuzaga kelişi mumkin.
ch01-f76.lead: Musbat teskari aloqa ba’zan foydali bölişi mumkin.

ch01-f77.text: Tuğruq — musbat teskari aloqa foydali bölgan yana bir holat. Baçadon qisqarişlari bola boşining baçadon böyni orqali itarilib çiqa boşlaşi uçun yetarliça kuçli bölganda, baçadon böynining çözilişi baçadon muskuli orqali baçadon tanasiga signallar yuboradi va yanada kuçliroq qisqarişlarga sabab böladi. Şunday qilib, baçadon qisqarişlari baçadon böynini çözadi, baçadon böynining çözilişi esa kuçliroq qisqarişlarni keltirib çiqaradi. Bu jarayon yetarliça kuçayganda bola tuğiladi. Agar qisqarişlar yetarliça kuçli bölmasa, ular odatda sönib qoladi va qayta boşlanişigaça bir neça kun ötadi.

ch01-f78.text: Musbat teskari aloqaning yana bir muhim qöllanilişi — nerv signallarining hosil bölişi. Nerv tolasi membranasining qözğatilişi natriy ionlarining nerv membranasidagi natriy kanallari orqali tola içiga biroz sizib kirişiga sabab böladi. Tolaga kirgan natriy ionlari membrana potensialini özgartiradi, bu esa öz navbatida kanallarning yanada köproq oçilişiga, potensialning yanada köproq özgarişiga, kanallarning yana ham köproq oçilişiga va hokazolarga olib keladi. Şunday qilib, kiçik siziş natriyning nerv tolasi içiga portlaşsimon kirişiga aylanadi va nerv harakat potensialini hosil qiladi. Bu harakat potensiali esa öz navbatida tolaning taşqi va içki yuzasi böylab elektr tokining oqişiga sabab böladi va qöşimça harakat potensiallarini yuzaga keltiradi. Bu jarayon nerv signali tolaning oxirigaça yetib borgunça davom etadi.

ch01-f79.text: Musbat teskari aloqa foydali bölgan har bir holatda u umumiy manfiy teskari aloqa jarayonining bir qismidir. Masalan, qon ivişida musbat teskari aloqali iviş jarayoni qonning me’yoriy hajmini saqlaşga xizmat qiluvçi manfiy teskari aloqa jarayonidir. Şuningdek, nerv signallarini keltirib çiqaruvçi musbat teskari aloqa nervlarga minglab manfiy teskari aloqali nerv boşqaruv tizimlarida iştirok etiş imkonini beradi.

ch01-f80.text: Boşqaruv tizimlarining murakkabroq turlari — oldindan boşqariş va adaptiv boşqariş

ch01-f81.text: Darslikning keyingi qismlarida nerv tizimini örganganimizda, bu tizimda özaro boğlangan juda köp boşqaruv mexanizmlari borligini köramiz. Ulardan ba’zilari yuqorida muhokama qilinganlarga öxşaş oddiy teskari aloqa tizimlaridir. Köpçiligi esa unday emas. Masalan, organizmning ba’zi harakatlari şunçalik tez sodir böladiki, harakatni boşqariş uçun nerv signallari organizmning periferik qismlaridan boş miyagaça borib, söngra yana periferiyaga qaytişiga vaqt yetmaydi. Şu sababli boş miya kerakli muskul qisqarişlarini yuzaga keltiriş uçun _oldindan boşqariş_ (feed-forward control) deb ataladigan mexanizmdan foydalanadi. Harakatlanayotgan qismlardan keladigan sezuvçi nerv signallari boş miyaga harakat töğri bajarilgan-bajarilmaganligi haqida xabar beradi. Agar töğri bajarilmagan bölsa, boş miya şu harakat _keyingi_ safar talab qilinganda muskullarga yuboradigan oldindan boşqaruvçi signallarni tuzatadi. Agar yana tuzatiş kerak bölsa, bu jarayon keyingi harakatlar uçun yana takrorlanadi. Bu jarayon _adaptiv boşqariş_ deb ataladi. Adaptiv boşqariş ma’lum ma’noda keçiktirilgan manfiy teskari aloqadir.

ch01-f82.text: Şunday qilib, organizmning teskari aloqali boşqaruv tizimlari qançalik murakkab bölişi mumkinligini köriş mumkin. Insonning hayoti ularning barçasiga boğliq. Şu sababli uşbu darslikning katta qismi ana şu hayot baxş etuvçi mexanizmlarni muhokama qilişga bağişlangan.

ch01-f84.text: Ba’zi fiziologik körsatkiçlar, masalan, plazmadagi kaliy, kalsiy va vodorod ionlari konsentratsiyalari qat’iy boşqarilsa-da, boşqalari, masalan, tana vazni va yoğ töqimasi miqdori turli odamlar orasida, hatto bitta odamda ham hayotning turli bosqiçlarida keng özgarib turadi. Arterial bosim, yurakning nasos faolligi, metabolizm tezligi, nerv tizimi faolligi, gormonlar va boşqa fiziologik körsatkiçlar biz harakatlanib, odatdagi kundalik faoliyat bilan şuğullanganimiz sari kun davomida özgarib turadi. Şu sababli “me’yoriy” qiymatlar haqida gapirganda, organizmning köplab boşqaruv tizimlari buzuvçi ta’sirlarga doimiy ravişda javob berib turişini hamda tana vazni va böyi, ovqatlaniş, yoş, jins, muhit, genetika va boşqa omillarga boğliq holda turli odamlar örtasida farqlar bölişi mumkinligini nazarda tutamiz.

ch01-f85.text: Soddalik uçun fiziologik funksiyalar muhokamasi köpinça vazni 70 kg bölgan “örtaça” yoş, ozğin erkakka qaratiladi. Biroq amerikalik erkakning örtaça vazni endi 70 kg emas; hozir u 88 kg dan ortiq, amerikalik ayolning örtaça vazni esa 76 kg dan ortiq bölib, bu 1960-yillardagi örtaça erkak vaznidan ham köp. Sönggi 40–50 yil davomida boşqa köpçilik sanoati rivojlangan mamlakatlarda ham tana vazni sezilarli darajada oşgan.

ch01-f86.text: Reproduktiv va gormonal funksiyalardan taşqari, köplab boşqa fiziologik funksiyalar va me’yoriy qiymatlar köpinça erkak fiziologiyasi nuqtai nazaridan muhokama qilinadi. Biroq erkak va ayol fiziologiyasi örtasida köpayiş bilan boğliq ravşan farqlardan taşqari ham aniq farqlar mavjud. Bu farqlar me’yoriy fiziologiyani tuşuniş uçun ham, kasalliklarni davolaş uçun ham muhim ahamiyatga ega bölişi mumkin.

ch01-f87.text: Fiziologiyadagi yoşga boğliq hamda etnik yoki irqiy farqlar ham tana tarkibiga, fiziologik boşqaruv tizimlariga va kasalliklar patofiziologiyasiga muhim ta’sir körsatadi. Masalan, ozğin yoş erkakda organizmdagi umumiy suv tana vaznining taxminan 60% ini taşkil qiladi. Inson ösib, qarib borgan sari bu uluş asta-sekin kamayadi; buning qisman sababi şundaki, qariş odatda skelet muskullari massasining kamayişi va yoğ massasining ortişi bilan keçadi. Qariş, şuningdek, ba’zi a’zolar va fiziologik boşqaruv tizimlarining funksiyasi va samaradorligi pasayişiga ham sabab bölişi mumkin.

ch01-f88.text: Fiziologik özgaruvçanlikning bu manbalari — jinsiy farqlar, qariş, etnik va irqiy farqlar — murakkab, biroq me’yoriy fiziologiya va kasalliklar patofiziologiyasini muhokama qilişda hisobga olinişi kerak bölgan muhim omillardir.

ch01-f90.text: Uşbu bobning asosiy maqsadi organizmning umumiy tuzilişini va uning turli qismlari uyğun işlaşini ta’minlovçi vositalarni qisqaça muhokama qiliş edi. Xulosa qilib aytganda, organizm aslida turli funksional tuzilmalarga birlaşgan, _taxminan 35–40 trillion hujayradan iborat ijtimoiy tuzum_ bölib, bu tuzilmalarning ba’zilari _a’zolar_ deb ataladi. Har bir funksional tuzilma _içki muhit_ deb ataladigan hujayradan taşqari suyuqlikda gomeostazni saqlaşga öz hissasini qöşadi. Içki muhitda me’yoriy şaroitlar saqlanib tursa, organizm hujayralari yaşaşda va töğri işlaşda davom etadi. Har bir hujayra gomeostazdan foyda köradi va öz navbatida har bir hujayra gomeostazni saqlaşga öz hissasini qöşadi. Bu özaro ta’sir bir yoki bir neçta funksional tizim öz uluşini bajariş qobiliyatini yöqotmagunça organizmning uzluksiz avtomatikligini ta’minlaydi. Bunday holat yuz berganda organizmning barça hujayralari zarar köradi. Funksiyaning keskin buzilişi ölimga, örtaça darajadagi buzilişi esa kasallikka olib keladi.
